mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 2.0% compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate borrowing costs remain low.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate decline exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals labor market overheating that triggers preemptive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE declines > 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust aggregate demand, driving corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in RSAFS and HOUST fails to produce positive 60-day returns in at least 60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals manufacturing contraction without monetary policy support, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In CPIAUCSL > 3.0% periods, INDPRO declines do not yield negative 20-day returns in >60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.02 for INDPRO in this regime.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly federal funds rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals aggressive monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS increases >0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A rising employment level (PAYEMS) supports consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days in expanding labor markets.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when PAYEMS is rising.

mechanism_narrative: In low-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL < 2.0%), rising consumer spending (RSAFS) signals sustainable economic growth without rate hike risks, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In CPIAUCSL < 2.0% periods, RSAFS increases do not yield positive 20-day returns in >60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.02 for RSAFS in this regime.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate broad economic contraction without policy support, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in INDPRO and HOUST fails to produce negative 5-day returns in >60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.02 for the interaction term over 3-year windows.
